## README INFO:

# DATASET 1 : Multimodal_Data.csv
 This data set has columns for:
 Site - Sites 1-15 (location)
 Visual_Cue - neutral (grey block), shape (fish model), move (moving fish model)
 Odor_Cue - water (control) or odor (anchovy juice)
 Combo - treatment combination (combines visual, odor cues, taste)
 Observer - name of researcher watching the footage (maya, gabby, dani)
 Date - Date of trial
 Zip_Color - color of zip tie on apparatus (pink, yellow, blue)
 Species - fish species that visited trial
 Max_Number	- maximum number of a species observed at a single time within the frame
 Arrival_Frame - time to arrive per species
 Time_to_Touch - time to touch the model with face per species
 Duration_Frame	- total duration at least 1 individual of a species was within the frame
 Duration_Facial_Contact - total duration at least 1 individual of a species had facial contact with the model
 Frame_Bite -  # of bites for frame per species
 Zip_Bite - # of bites for zip ties per species
 Total_Structure_Bite - Frame + Zip bites, any part of apparatus
 Model_Bite	- # of bites for visual model per species
 Selfie - # of camera investigations per species
 Non-Eel_SubAdult	- max number of observed juvenile individuals per species
 Non-Eel_Adult	Notes	- max number of observed adult individuals per species
 
# DATASET 2: Multi_YN.csv
This dataset pulls info from dataset 1 to track the frequency each species visited a particular treatment at a particular site to track the % of times a species arrived - if a species showed up for a trial, we recorded that as a "yes", and if they did not that is a "no". 

This datset contains columns:
Site - Sites 1-15 (location)
Combo - treatment combination (combines visual, odor cues, taste)
Zip_Color - color of zip tie on apparatus (pink, yellow, blue)
Kelp_Bass - yes/no if a kelp bass showed up
Moray - yes/no if a moray showed up
Garibaldi - yes/no if a garibaldi showed up
Any_Fish? - yes/no if any of the species showed up

# Reading in the Datasets 
```{r - Reading in datasets}

### -------- DATASET 1 -----------

Multimodal <- read.csv("Data/Multimodal_Data.csv")

# Look at it!
head(Multimodal)

#Making "characters" into "factors":
Multimodal$Site = factor(Multimodal$Site)
Multimodal$Visual_Cue = factor(Multimodal$Visual_Cue)
Multimodal$Odor_Cue = factor(Multimodal$Odor_Cue)
Multimodal$Combo = factor(Multimodal$Combo)
Multimodal$Zip_Color = factor(Multimodal$Zip_Color)
Multimodal$Species = factor(Multimodal$Species)

# Look at it!
head(Multimodal)

species_count <- Multimodal %>%
  group_by(Species) %>%
  summarise(count = n())

Species_Per <- species_count %>% 
  group_by(Species) %>% 
  count/105




#### ------- DATASET 2 - Yes/No Data ---------

MultiYN  <- read.csv("Data/Multi_YN.csv")

# Making all characters factors
MultiYN <-MultiYN %>%
  mutate_if(is.character, as.factor) %>% 
  mutate(across(c(Kelp_Bass, Garibaldi, Moray), ~ as.numeric(. == "yes"))) %>% 
  rename("Kelp Bass" = Kelp_Bass, "Chemical Cue"= Chemical_Cue) 

# Look at it:
head(MultiYN)

# Reshape to long format for future us
MultiYN_long <- MultiYN %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(`Kelp Bass`, Garibaldi, Moray), 
               names_to = "Species", # new column named "Species" - contains species names
               values_to = "Visited") # new column named "Visited" - contains yes or no

# Look at it:
head(MultiYN_long)
```
# 1. DID THEY ARRIVE? 

This uses the MultiYN dataset, for "yes" something arrived or "no" something did not arrive

### Stats - Within Species Arrival 

Kelp Bass
```{r - Arrival Kelp Bass}
# Kelp Bass
kelpbass_summary <- MultiYN %>%
  group_by(Combo) %>%
  summarise(
    visits = sum(`Kelp Bass`),                      # total visits (number of 1's)
    proportion = mean(`Kelp Bass`),                 # proportion of 1's
    sd = sd(`Kelp Bass`),                           # standard deviation
    se = sd / sqrt(n())                             # standard error
  )

print(kelpbass_summary)



#####

# Build a contingency table: counts of yes/no by treatment
kelp_table <- table(MultiYN$Combo, MultiYN$`Kelp Bass`)
chisq.test(kelp_table)

fisher.test(kelp_table)

# Get all unique treatment combos
combos <- unique(MultiYN$Combo)

# Create empty data frame to store results
fisher_results <- data.frame(
  Combo1 = character(),
  Combo2 = character(),
  p_value = numeric(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Loop over all unique pairwise combinations
for(i in 1:(length(combos) - 1)) {
  for(j in (i + 1):length(combos)) {
    
    # Filter data for the two combos
    sub_data <- MultiYN %>% filter(Combo %in% c(combos[i], combos[j]))
    
    # Run Fisher's Exact Test
    ft <- fisher.test(table(sub_data$Combo, sub_data$`Kelp Bass`))
    
    # Store the result
    fisher_results <- rbind(
      fisher_results,
      data.frame(
        Combo1 = combos[i],
        Combo2 = combos[j],
        p_value = ft$p.value
      )
    )
  }
}

# Add significance stars
fisher_results <- fisher_results %>%
  mutate(significance = case_when(
    p_value <= 0.001 ~ "***",
    p_value <= 0.01 ~ "**",
    p_value <= 0.05 ~ "*",
    TRUE ~ ""
  )) %>%
  arrange(p_value)

# View the table
print(fisher_results)

```

### Stats - Between Species


Oops - Between species attempt
```{r}
# Create a list of unique treatment combos
# Get list of unique combos
combos <- unique(MultiYN$Combo)

# Create empty dataframe to store results
pairwise_species_results <- data.frame(
  Combo = character(),
  Species1 = character(),
  Species2 = character(),
  p_value = numeric(),
  test_type = character(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Loop over each treatment combo
for (combo in combos) {
  sub_data <- MultiYN %>% filter(Combo == combo)
  
  # Create a list of species columns
  species_list <- list(
    Garibaldi = sub_data$Garibaldi,
    KelpBass = sub_data$KelpBass,
    Moray = sub_data$Moray
  )
  
  species_names <- names(species_list)
  
  # All pairwise combinations of species
  for (i in 1:(length(species_list) - 1)) {
    for (j in (i + 1):length(species_list)) {
      
      # Extract yes/no counts for both species
      species1_vals <- species_list[[i]]
      species2_vals <- species_list[[j]]
      
      # Create 2x2 contingency table
      contingency_table <- matrix(
        c(
          sum(species1_vals == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
          sum(species1_vals == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
          sum(species2_vals == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
          sum(species2_vals == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
        ),
        nrow = 2,
        byrow = TRUE
      )
      rownames(contingency_table) <- c(species_names[i], species_names[j])
      colnames(contingency_table) <- c("Yes", "No")
      
      # Run Fisher's Exact Test
      test_result <- fisher.test(contingency_table)
      
      # Store result
      pairwise_species_results <- rbind(
        pairwise_species_results,
        data.frame(
          Combo = combo,
          Species1 = species_names[i],
          Species2 = species_names[j],
          p_value = test_result$p.value,
          test_type = "Fisher"
        )
      )
    }
  }
}

# Add significance stars
pairwise_species_results <- pairwise_species_results %>%
  mutate(significance = case_when(
    p_value <= 0.001 ~ "***",
    p_value <= 0.01 ~ "**",
    p_value <= 0.05 ~ "*",
    TRUE ~ ""
  )) %>%
  arrange(Combo, p_value)

# View results
print(pairwise_species_results)

```






### Graphic Prep - Arrival Y/N 
```{r Arrival? Yes.No}

# Calculate percentage visitation per treatment for each species
Arrival_summary <- MultiYN_long %>%
  group_by(Visual_Cue, `Chemical Cue`, Combo, Species) %>%
  summarize(
    Percent_Visited = mean(Visited == "1") * 100,
    sd = sd(Visited == "1", na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    se = sd / sqrt(n)
  )

Arrival_summary
```

### Graphic - Arrival Y/N
```{r Arrival Y/N Graphic}

# Creating a data frame with pairwise significance: 
Arrvival_Signif <- tribble(
  ~Visual_Cue,    ~`Chemical Cue`,          ~Species,     ~Signif,
  "Neutral",        "control",            "Kelp Bass",      "a",    
  "Shape",          "control",            "Kelp Bass",      "a",   
  "Move",            "control",           "Kelp Bass",      "a",    
  "Neutral",          "odor",             "Kelp Bass",      "b",    
  "Shape",             "odor",            "Kelp Bass",      "b",   
  "Move",             "odor",             "Kelp Bass",      "b", 
  "Neutral",         "odor+taste",         "Kelp Bass",      "b", 
  "Neutral",        "control",            "Moray",          "a",    
  "Shape",          "control",            "Moray",          "a",   
  "Move",            "control",           "Moray",          "a",    
  "Neutral",          "odor",             "Moray",          "b",    
  "Shape",             "odor",            "Moray",          "b",   
  "Move",             "odor",             "Moray",          "b", 
  "Neutral",         "odor+taste",           "Moray",        "b" 
) %>% 
  left_join(transmute(Arrival_summary, Visual_Cue, `Chemical Cue`, Species, Percent_Visited, se),
            by = c("Visual_Cue", "Chemical Cue", "Species")) %>% 
  mutate(y = Percent_Visited + se + 10)  # Ensures unique y value per bar




ArrivalGraphic = 
  Arrival_summary  %>% 
  filter(Species %in% c("Kelp Bass", "Moray")) %>% 
  mutate(Visual_Cue = fct_relevel(Visual_Cue, "Neutral", "Shape", "Move")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Visual_Cue, y = Percent_Visited, fill = `Chemical Cue`)) + 
  geom_bar(stat ="identity", 
           color = "black", 
           position = position_dodge()) +
# error bar 
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Percent_Visited - sd, ymax = Percent_Visited + sd), 
                width = 0.25,
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.9))+
# Adding Significance Labels
geom_text(data = Arrvival_Signif, 
          aes(x = Visual_Cue, y = y, label = Signif, fill = `Chemical Cue`), 
          position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), 
          size = 3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey", "#FAA275", "#B56576", "#363457")) +
  #scale_x_discrete(labels = new_labels) +
  theme_classic() +
  facet_wrap(. ~ Species, nrow = 1)+
  ggtitle("") +
   theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 20, hjust = 0.5, family = "Lucida Grande", color = "#363457")) +
  labs(y = "% Trials Visited", x = "") +
  theme (axis.text.x = element_text(size = 0, angle=0, family = "Lucida Grande"), 
         axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8, family = "Lucida Grande"),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10, family = "Lucida Grande",face = "bold", margin = margin(r = 3)),
         legend.position="none",
         panel.spacing.x = unit(3, "lines"),
         strip.background = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = "#363457"),
         strip.placement = "inside",
         strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face="bold", color = "white", family = "Lucida Grande"))
ArrivalGraphic 


ggsave("ArrivalGraph.png", plot = ArrivalGraphic, width = 5, height = 5, units = "in", dpi = 500)
```

## 2. DURATION IN FRAME
Using a glmm with a Gamma distribution, with a post-hoc pairwaise comparison using the tukey method 

#### Stats - Within Species
```{r Stats Duration - Within Species}
# --------------------------- #
#     DURATION IN FRAME      #
# --------------------------- #

# 🔸 Garibaldi 🔸

# Fit the gamma GLMM with random intercepts
Dur_Garibaldi <- glmer(Duration_Frame ~ Combo + (1 | Site),
                          data = Garibaldi,
                          family = Gamma(link = "log"))
# Print model summary
summary(Dur_Garibaldi)

# Estimated marginal means and pairwise comparisons 
EMMS_Dur_Garibaldi <- emmeans(Dur_Garibaldi, "Combo")
pairs(EMMS_Dur_Garibaldi)


# Checking Model Fit
# Simulate residuals
sim_res <- simulateResiduals(Dur_Garibaldi)

# Plot residuals
plot(sim_res)

# Test for overdispersion
testDispersion(sim_res)

# Test for uniformity of residuals
testUniformity(sim_res)

# Test for zero-inflation (if applicable)
# testZeroInflation(sim_res)

# 🏁 Kelp Bass 🏁

# Fit the gamma GLMM with random intercepts
Dur_KelpBass <- glmer(Duration_Frame ~ Combo + (1 | Site),
                          data = KelpBass,
                          family = Gamma(link = "log"))

# Print model summary
summary(Dur_KelpBass)

# Estimated marginal means and pairwise comparisons 
EMMS_Dur_KelpBass <- emmeans(Dur_KelpBass, "Combo")
pairs(EMMS_Dur_KelpBass)


# Checking Model Fit
shapiro.test(residuals(Dur_KelpBass))
### SHAPIRO test is W = 0.96952, p-value = 0.06412
### The residuals from your model do not significantly deviate from normality based on this test, suggesting that the assumption of normality holds reasonably well

# Simulate residuals
sim_res <- simulateResiduals(Dur_KelpBass)

# Plot residuals
plot(sim_res)

# Test for overdispersion
testDispersion(sim_res)

# Test for uniformity of residuals
testUniformity(sim_res)

# Moray 🪝

MorayN <- Moray %>%
  group_by(Combo) %>%  # Replace 'Treatment' with the actual column name for your treatments
  filter(n() > 1) %>%      # Keeps only groups where the count of rows is greater than 1
  ungroup()                # Removes the grouping structure from the dataframe

# Fit the gamma GLMM with random intercepts
Dur_Moray <- glmer(Duration_Frame ~ Combo + (1 | Site),
                          data = MorayN,
                          family = Gamma(link = "log"))

# Print model summary
summary(Dur_Moray)

# Estimated marginal means and pairwise comparisons 
EMMS_Dur_Moray <- emmeans(Dur_Moray, "Combo")
pairs(EMMS_Dur_Moray)

# Checking Model Fit
shapiro.test(residuals(Dur_Moray))
### SHAPIRO test is W = 0.9378, p-value = 0.0197
### The residuals from your model do not significantly deviate from normality based on this test, suggesting that the assumption of normality holds reasonably well

# Simulate residuals
sim_res <- simulateResiduals(Dur_Moray)

# Plot residuals
plot(sim_res)

# Test for overdispersion
testDispersion(sim_res)

# Test for uniformity of residuals
testUniformity(sim_res)
```

## 3. FACIAL CONTACT DURATION 
 --------------------------- 
  FACIAL CONTACT DURATION   
 --------------------------- 
Using a glmm with a Gamma distribution, with a post-hoc pairwaise comparison using the tukey method -- this is comparing the duration of time fish spent making prolonged facial contact with the target. "Prolonged" in that it is not a distince, rapid bite - but rubbing of the face on the target 

#### Stats - Within Species - compares all treatements within a single species
```{r Stats Facial Contact Duration}
# ------------------------------------------- #
#   FACIAL CONTACT DURATION - WITHIN SPECIES  #
# ------------------------------------------- #

# 🔸 Garibaldi 🔸
### NO CONTACT 
# Fit the gamma GLMM with random intercepts

                          #data = Garibaldi,
                          #family = Gamma(link = "log"))
# Print model summary

#-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

KelpBass <- KelpBass %>%
  mutate(Duration_Facial_Contact = Duration_Facial_Contact + 0.001)  # Add a small constant value  


FaceDur_KelpBass <- glm(Duration_Facial_Contact ~ Combo,
                          data = KelpBass,
                          family = Gamma(link = "log"))

# Print model summary
summary(FaceDur_KelpBass)

# Estimated marginal means and pairwise comparisons

pairs(EMMS_FaceDur_KelpBass)

testDispersion(sim_res)

# Test for uniformity of residuals
testUniformity(sim_res)
```

### Stats - Max Number
```{r Stats Max Number}
# --------------------------- #
#   MAX NUMBER INDIVIDUALS  #
# --------------------------- #

# 🔸 Garibaldi 🔸

# Fit a Poisson GLMM -- Shows underdispersion so we are using a quassi-poisson, with no random effects (see notes in Kelp Bass)
# test_poisson <- glmer(Max_Number ~ Combo + (1|Site), family = poisson, data = Garibaldi)

# Calculate overdispersion ratio
#overdispersion_ratio <- sum(residuals(test_poisson, type = "pearson")^2) / df.residual(test_poisson)
# print(overdispersion_ratio)

# OUTPUT: 
# > print(overdispersion_ratio)
# [1] 0.1419935
# This shows underdispersion --  (This suggests that the variance is smaller than what would be expected under a Poisson distribution). So we are using a Quasi-Poisson because this lessens (?) assumption that variance and mean are equal 

### Fit a SIMPLE quasi-Poisson model without random effects
Max_Garibaldi <- glm(Max_Number ~ Combo, family = quasipoisson, data = Garibaldi)
summary(Max_Garibaldi)  # Check the summary for convergence issues

# Estimated marginal means and pairwise comparisons 
EMMS_Max_Garibaldi <- emmeans(Max_Garibaldi, "Combo")
pairs(EMMS_Max_Garibaldi )    # NO SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCES

#Fit the model with quasi-Poisson with Site as random effect -- NOT using this code
Max_Garibaldi <- glmmPQL(Max_Number ~ Combo, random = ~1 | Site, family = quasipoisson, data = Garibaldi)

# Print model summary
summary(Max_Garibaldi)

# Estimated marginal means and pairwise comparisons 
#EMMS_Max_Garibaldi <- emmeans(Max_Garibaldi, "Combo")
# pairs(EMMS_Max_Garibaldi)

#-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 🏁 Kelp Bass 🏁

# We compared two models with quasipoisson distributions; one with site as a random effect, and one without - The glm model is simpler and provides more complete information about deviance and the significance of fixed effects, making it easier to interpret.The glmmPQL model introduces random effects, but the tiny standard deviation of the random intercept may indicate that it is not contributing meaningfully to the model.

### Fit a SIMPLE quasi-Poisson model without random effects
Max_KelpBass <- glm(Max_Number ~ Combo, family = quasipoisson, data = KelpBass)
summary(Max_KelpBass)  # Check the summary for convergence issues

# Estimated marginal means and pairwise comparisons 
EMMS_Max_Kelpbass<- emmeans(Max_KelpBass, "Combo")
pairs(EMMS_Max_Kelpbass)


### Fit a model WITH random effects -- NOT using this one

# Print model summary

# Estimated marginal means and pairwise comparisons
```

```{r - Max Number}
  mutate(Visual_Cue = factor(Visual_Cue, levels = c("neutral", "shape", "move")))

MaxIndData 


# Update DurationFacial_Signif with smaller offset
MaxInd_Signif <- tribble(
  ~Visual_Cue,    ~`Chemical Cue`,          ~Species,     ~Signif,
  "neutral",        "control",            "Garibaldi",      "a",    
  "shape",          "control",            "Garibaldi",      "a",   
  "move",            "control",           "Garibaldi",      "a",    
  "neutral",          "odor",             "Garibaldi",      "a",    
  "shape",             "odor",            "Garibaldi",      "",   
  "move",             "odor",             "Garibaldi",      "a", 
  "neutral",         "odor+skin",         "Garibaldi",      "a",
  "neutral",        "control",            "Kelp Bass",      "X",    
  "shape",          "control",            "Kelp Bass",      "a",   
  "move",            "control",           "Kelp Bass",      "X",    
  "neutral",          "odor",             "Kelp Bass",      "a",    
  "shape",             "odor",            "Kelp Bass",      "b",   
  "move",             "odor",             "Kelp Bass",      "d", 
  "neutral",         "odor+skin",         "Kelp Bass",      "b",
  "neutral",        "control",            "Moray",          "",    
  "shape",          "control",            "Moray",          "",   
  "move",            "control",           "Moray",          "",    
  "neutral",          "odor",             "Moray",          "a",    
  "shape",             "odor",            "Moray",          "a",   
  "move",             "odor",             "Moray",          "a", 
  "neutral",         "odor+skin",         "Moray",          "a" 
) %>% 
  left_join(transmute(MaxIndData, Visual_Cue, `Chemical Cue`, Species, mean, se),
            by = c("Visual_Cue", "Chemical Cue", "Species")) 

MaxInd_Signif  <- MaxInd_Signif  %>% 
  group_by(Species) %>% 
  mutate(y = mean + se + 0.3 * max(mean))  # Offset relative to the max mean per panel


MaxGraphic <- MaxIndData  %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Visual_Cue, y = mean, fill = `Chemical Cue`)) + 
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", 
           color = "black", 
           width = 0.9,
           position = position_dodge(0.9)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se), 
                width = 0.25,
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
  geom_text(data = MaxInd_Signif, 
            aes(x = Visual_Cue, y = y, label = Signif, fill = `Chemical Cue`), 
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), 
            size = 3, inherit.aes = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey", "#FAA275", "#B56576", "#363457")) +
  #scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .5))) +
  theme_classic() +
  facet_wrap(. ~ Species, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +  # Free y-axis for better scaling
  ggtitle("") +
  labs(y = "Maximum Individuals Observed Per Trial", x = "") +
   theme (axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, angle=0, family = "Lucida Grande"), 
         axis.text.y = element_text(size = 15, family = "Lucida Grande"),
         axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20, family = "Lucida Grande", margin = margin(r = 10)),
         axis.title.x = element_text(size = 20, family = "Lucida Grande", margin = margin(t = 55)),
         legend.position="none",
         panel.spacing.x = unit(2, "lines"),
         #plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 25, color = "black", family = "Lucida Grande", margin = margin(b = 20)),
         strip.background = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = "#363457"),
         strip.placement = "inside",
         strip.text = element_text(size = 16, face="bold", color = "white", family = "Lucida Grande"))

MaxGraphic

# Save the ggplot as a PNG file
ggsave("MaxGraphic.png", plot = MaxGraphic, width = 5, height = 10, units = "in", dpi = 500)

```

#### Stats - Between Species
```{r States Duration - Between Species}

# Fit the gamma GLMM with random intercepts
Bite_CubeWater <- glm(Model_Bite ~ Species, data = CubeWater, family = poisson)

summary(Bite_CubeWater)

# Estimated marginal means and pairwise comparisons

pairs(EMMS_Bite_CubeWater)

# Checking Model Fit

sim_res <- simulateResiduals(Bite_CubeWater)
# Plot residuals
plot(sim_res)
# Test for overdispersion
testDispersion(sim_res)
# Test for uniformity of residuals
testUniformity(sim_res)
```
